Welcome to Our Primary School
I hope our website gives you a ‘flavour’ of our fantastic school, which is very proud to be part of Pickwick Academy Trust. We truly believe that Greentrees is a very special place where everyone works together to ensure that our pupils are successful. This collaborative effort is key to our success – staff, governors, pupils and their families working in true partnership towards a shared vision. Children feel safe, supported and motivated to achieve their very best.
Visit our class pages to find out about the exciting learning the children are engaged in, including examples of their work. Our website is also home to a vast amount of important information, including our weekly newsletter and key dates for the diary.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website. If you require any further help or information, please contact the school office.
Mr Alan Geary, Headteacher

At Greentrees, we consider how we demonstrate the fundamental British Values in our daily lives. We understand that we live in a diverse society and that we can all live together peacefully. British Values help us to understand how we can become the best citizens we can be within our communities and the wider multicultural world.

Collective Worship
Reflection Time is an inclusive part of school life and reflects our caring ethos and commitment to developing the whole child. It contributes to pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development, helping them to develop a greater understanding of themselves, others and the world around them. Through stories, discussion, music, celebration and moments of quiet reflection, children are encouraged to think deeply, appreciate different perspectives and develop a sense of wonder about the world.
Our Reflection Time programme is rooted in the broad Christian tradition and includes festivals and events from the Christian calendar. We also learn about and celebrate significant festivals and events from other faiths and cultures, helping pupils to develop respect, understanding and appreciation of the diverse communities in which we live. Reflection Time supports our school vision, promotes our shared values and encourages children to recognise how they can make a positive difference to others and to the wider world.
Parents have the legal right to withdraw their child from Collective Worship. However, we hope this would be a last resort due to the important role Reflection Time plays in promoting inclusion, community spirit, reflection and personal development. If parents are considering withdrawing their child, they should first contact the school office to arrange a meeting with the Headteacher. This provides an opportunity to discuss the content and purpose of Reflection Time, ask any questions and, if desired, observe an example of Collective Worship.
If parents choose to withdraw their child from all or part of Collective Worship, this request should be made to the Headteacher. No reason needs to be given for the decision. The school will make appropriate arrangements for the supervision of any pupil who is withdrawn.
Please note that the right to withdraw applies only to Collective Worship. It does not extend to other aspects of school life or the curriculum where discussions about beliefs, values, faiths, cultures and worldviews may arise, including within subjects such as Religious Education, History, Geography and PSHE.

The school week for pupils at Greentrees Primary School is 32.5 hours.
All pupils have a 15-minute morning break. Lunch is from 12:00pm to 1:00pm for all pupils.
Pupils should arrive promptly to ensure they are ready to begin learning at the start of the school day.

At Greentrees, we follow a systematic synthetic phonics approach in EYFS and Key Stage 1. We use Phonics Shed, a validated, narrrative-driven and multi-sensory phonics programme. Daily phonics lessons make use of the scheme’s teaching books, e-books, reading books, songs, letter formation animations and interactive games to engage children and support their learning.
The Phonics Shed programme also provides consolidation and intervention materials for pupils in EYFS, KS1 and KS2 who require additional support, helping to ensure that all children keep up with their phonics development.
We use the assessment tools within Phonics Shed to regularly assess attainment and progress in phonics. Children in KS1, alongside any KS2 pupils who have not yet met the expected standard in the Phonics Screening Check, are assessed during the fifth week of each term. Assessment outcomes enable teachers to identify gaps in pupils’ phonics knowledge, evaluate the effectiveness of teaching, and plan targeted interventions to ensure that all children make strong progress.
Children take home books from the Phonics Shed decodable reading scheme. These are carefully matched to the grapheme-phoneme correspondences (GPCs) they have been taught in school, enabling them to practise and apply their developing phonics knowledge with confidence.
Some books also contain Common Exception Words (CEWs). These are frequently used words that cannot always be fully decoded using the phonics knowledge children have learnt so far, such as the, to, of and so. Children are taught to use their phonics knowledge for the parts of the word they can decode and to recognise the parts that are not yet decodable. This approach enables them to access and enjoy a wider range of texts more quickly.
In addition to their decodable reading book, children also take home a Share with Me book, identified by a star sticker on the front cover. These books are intended to be enjoyed together with an adult and may not be fully decodable for the child. They help to develop a love of reading, build vocabulary and support comprehension skills such as retrieving information, predicting and discussing what has been read.
Each year group has access to a set of 50 Recommended Reads, complied by the Books for Topics website. Each collection contains 50 carefully selected books chosen to promote reading for pleasure. The books are age-appropriate and accessible, representing a wide range of genres and styles, including fiction, picture books, non-fiction, poetry and graphic novels.
The collections cater for different interests and reading preferences, featuring both timeless classics and contemporary favourites. They also reflect a diverse range of characters, experiences and settings, ensuring that all children are able to see themselves in books while also learning about the lives and experiences of others.

The Multiplication Tables Check, or MTC, is a statutory assessment for Year 4 pupils in England to assess their fluency in recalling multiplication facts. The assessment takes place within a designated two-week window in June. The test is an online, on-screen assessment where pupils have 6 seconds to answer 25 questions. The questions posed will be drawn from all multiplication tables at random. There will always be questions from the 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12 multiplication tables in each check. There will be no questions from the 1 times table. The 6, 7, 8, 9 and 12 times tables are more likely to be asked.
The following 11 multiplication questions are most likely to appear in the check:
6 x 6, 6 x 7, 6 x 8, 6 x 9, 6 x 12
7 x 8, 7 x 9, 7 x 12
Access Arrangements:
Children with additional needs, who have similar provision in their day-to-day learning at school, may be provided with specific arrangements including: colour contrast adjustment, font size adjustment, ‘next’ button (as an alternative to a 3-second pause, an adult to input answers, a question reader.
Prior to the check, pupils will be well-prepared in school. In Years 3 and 4 all tables facts are learnt progressively as a memorised phrase by repeating the sound pattern out loud. This happens daily using printed times table booklets. Rarely do these booklets get used in their entirety. We encourage pupils to take them home when the next booklet is started to encourage additional practice. We also encourage pupils to use Mathsframe as often as possible at home and in school. This is a website which looks very similar to the format of the MTC. This website allows pupils to choose a particular multiplication table or to try all times tables mixed (as questions will be posed in the real MTC). We recommend the default setting of answering 25 questions with 6 seconds to respond because this aligns with the check.
We aim to host two information sessions for Year 4 parents about the MTC in April each year. Please do all you can to attend one of these session to support us in preparing your child for this check.
